column1: # Divergence registry: deliberate differences from MuJoCo 3.5.0, each with the test that shows it. Every
# `divergence=<ID>` note in verdicts.tsv names an ID here (mujoco_conformance/layer_e_census.rs checks it);
# a row no note names is a difference no census doc exercises.
# kind: stricter (we refuse what MuJoCo accepts) · limitation (MuJoCo does what we cannot) ·
#       no-effect (accepted, with no effect) · lenient (we load where MuJoCo wrongly refuses) ·
#       wrong-value (MuJoCo computes a wrong value; the test shows ours is right) ·
#       extension (a quantity MuJoCo does not have).

column3: MuJoCo
column4: ours

column3: loads a NaN or an infinity written in a number (measured: a body's pos and quat, a joint's axis, damping and range, a geom's friction, a motor's ctrlrange, keyframe values, a tendon's springlength, <option> numbers, a fixed tendon's joint coef, an infinite geom size, a NaN written with a payload such as nan(1)), except where its compiler refuses the value (measured: a NaN geom size, a capsule's NaN fromto, a non-finite mesh vertex, a NaN mass or density on a moving body); refuses a number past its type's range ("number is too large": a double's, or a float's for an attribute it reads as float)
column4: refuses a NaN or an infinity written in any number it reads, naming the element and attribute, and a number past its type's range as MuJoCo refuses it; a model built in code or read from .mjb is checked only where validation and the builder check it: keyframe values, a fixed tendon's joint coef, an inertial's mass and diaginertia, a geom's size and fromto, a site's size, and the <option> numbers timestep, tolerance, impratio, regularization, friction_smoothing, gravity, wind, density, viscosity and an o_margin of 0 or more

column4: takes the sample at the step's start state, before the stages: a sensor delayed by one timestep reads, bit for bit, the undelayed value one step earlier, under every integrator

column3: under RK4, wakes a sleeping tree that nothing touched, the step after it sleeps: mj_advance's sleep step evaluates the forward pass again from the velocity stage (engine_forward.c:899-905), so the tree keeps the last stage's frames while its qpos is the step's start, which the next kinematics find changed (engine_core_smooth.c:163-179); and the stages integrate a sleeping dof with the stale acceleration it keeps (:1086-1090), so the stage's forward pass finds the tree moving (engine_sleep.c:124-153). The sleep step's sensors read the last stage's positions (a resting box: 584 sleep changes in 3,000 steps; a pendulum beside it, on that step, 0.116 off)
column4: holds a tree asleep at the step's start there through the stages and the advance until a stage's forward pass wakes it (a contact, say; from that stage on it takes each stage's acceleration, as MuJoCo's, and the stages it was held through count as 0, the acceleration they moved it with, where MuJoCo's stages moved it with the one it kept), and evaluates the sleep step's forward pass from the position stage, so collision and a contact filter callback run once more on that step than in MuJoCo's, whose pass starts from the velocity stage: the tree sleeps once and stays asleep, its frames those of its qpos, the sleep step's sensors those of the step's start state

column3: with islands, copies an island's forces back to the rows and not their states (engine_forward.c:796-798; the island solve's states are in iefc_state, engine_solver.c:940), so efc_state is what the warmstart left, made at qacc_smooth (:662), or unset with the warmstart disabled: a row's state can contradict its own force (a friction-loss row inside its band reads LinearPos)

column3: takes acos of the cosine between the directions of a sphere or cylinder wrap's two tangent points unclamped (length_circle, engine_util_misc.c:55-71): where the cosine rounds past 1, on a segment grazing a sphere, the tendon's length is NaN; where it is exactly 1, on a segment tangent to a sphere, its acos is 0 and the cross product's sign may still ask for the long way round: the length is the straight segment's plus 2πr (ledger L185); one ulp below 1 the sign can still ask for the long way round (80 sphere and 108 cylinder wraps of the chunk 3e-2 review's 3,000 tangent segments)
column4: clamps the cosine to [-1, 1], and where it is 1 or rounds past it takes the arc as 0, never the long way round (at exactly 1 too, by the wrong-value rule): the length is finite, within the arc the clamp drops of the straight segment's (at most the radius times 1.67e-8 over 7,200 grazing segments, the chunk 3e-1 review's sweep); on the test's first two segments the straight segment's to 0 and 2.0e-12 (of 0.3 and 20); on the test's tangent sphere segment, MuJoCo's less 2πr; one ulp below 1 it goes the long way round as MuJoCo's does (recorded, not changed: the project lead's call, 2026-10-18)

column3: mj_rne writes the awake dofs only (engine_core_smooth.c:2481-2484) and mj_inverseSkip adds the rest of the sum to qfrc_inverse at every dof (engine_inverse.c:238-241), so a sleeping dof's qfrc_inverse grows call by call (a box asleep on a plane after resting: -19.62, -39.24, -58.86 on its vertical dof, where the forward pass applied 0; a box asleep from the reset keeps qacc 0 and reads 0); mjd_inverseFD's centre and points add to it in turn (DfDa -1.962e7 there) and a qpos nudge that wakes a tree carries into its later points
column4: a sleeping dof's qfrc_inverse is the forces applied there, qfrc_applied + qfrc_actuator + J'*xfrc_applied, call after call, whatever qacc it keeps (both boxes: 0), so a sleeping tree adds nothing to fwdinv's solver_fwdinv[1]; mjd_inverse_fd takes each point from the centre's whole state, its sleep state included, so DfDa is 0 at a sleeping dof's row

column3: mjd_smooth_vel clears qDeriv at the awake rows only (engine_derivative.c:1793-1800, mju_zeroSparse over dof_awake_ind), so an awake tendon over a sleeping dof adds its -b·J² to that dof's row every step (-0.27, -0.54, -0.81, -1.08); the implicit step factors the awake rows only

column3: keeps the fourth point's weight in GJK's S3D as an earlier face set it (engine_collision_gjk.c:633-643), so the weights can sum past 1; in the distance sensor mjc_ccd then takes some pairs that are apart as touching (:2298-2299) and reads 0, two boxes or meshes most often (stopped at a tolerance of 0, discreteGeoms, :159-167; in the chunk 3e-2 review's random sample, 261 of 4,227 turned box pairs apart and 106 of 36,923 other pairs of boxes, ellipsoids and cylinders; in chunk 3e-3's, 3 of 150 box-mesh and 3 of 150 mesh-mesh pairs apart); and mjc_Convex, which calls the same mjc_ccd, gives a sphere's contact with an ellipsoid, and a capsule's with an ellipsoid or a cylinder, another depth and normal at some poses (in chunk 3e-3's review, 55, 64 and 78 of 40,000 random sphere-ellipsoid, capsule-cylinder and capsule-ellipsoid poses; on 18 of them the depth up to 2.5e-5 apart, the normal up to 1.1e-2 rad, and once one contact where MuJoCo's passes list two)
column4: sets that weight to 0 (cf-geometry's gjk_distance, and sim-core's port of mjc_ccd, which the contacts and the sensor share): the sensor reads the pair's distance (on the test's three box pairs, the exact distance within 1e-12; on its four mesh pairs, MuJoCo's own reading with the second body moved 1e-9, within 3e-9); on the test's six sphere-ellipsoid contacts the distance is within 3.0e-8 of the exact one, where MuJoCo's parts by 5.8e-7 to 3.1e-6

column3: builds a mesh's convex hull with qhull (mjCMesh::MakeGraph), whose vertex and face order set its hill climb's graph (mjc_hillclimbSupport, engine_collision_convex.c:383-430) and the order MakePolygons (user_mesh.cc:2949-3005) merges the hull's faces in, so which polygons it makes where neighbouring faces lie within the merge tolerance, the corner each polygon's path starts at, and their order; the multi-contact (engine_collision_gjk.c:1442-2184) clips those polygons, keeps a face's first 150 corners from that start (mjMAX_POLYVERT) and prunes a clipped face of more than four corners to four from it (polygonQuad, :1466-1509); and mjc_PlaneConvex lists a plane's further contacts with a mesh among the first vertex's neighbours in that graph's order, up to two (engine_collision_convex.c:1108-1135), the first vertex where mjccd_support's hill climb on it ends (:624-667), on a face lying on the plane one of its tied corners
column4: takes the graph and the polygons from our own hull (book 01-decisions: the hull is matched as sets), merged as MuJoCo merges (from MuJoCo's own hull faces, MuJoCo's polygons); from ours a polygon's path can start at another corner and, where faces lie within the merge tolerance, the polygons can differ, so mesh contacts under MULTICCD can differ: on the golden's 64 box-mesh and mesh-mesh cases every count and distance is MuJoCo's and 19 keep other corners; at the test's poses a box resting on a mesh face gets MuJoCo's four contacts in another order, the mesh on itself two contacts more than 1e-2 from MuJoCo's, and at a margin a depth 2.2e-7 from MuJoCo's; in chunk 3e-3's review, faces parallel to an axis put contacts up to 3.8e-2 off and one count at 4 where MuJoCo lists 5, and on large faces of many corners MuJoCo's hill climb stops short of the furthest vertex where ours does not (distances up to 6.1e-8 apart); a plane and a mesh, on the golden's 168 plane-mesh cases on our hull's graph: 47 differ from MuJoCo's (4 in count, positions up to 0.14 apart, distances up to 2.7e-2), the first contact listed whenever MuJoCo's is, at its distance within 1e-16, on 15 face-down poses at another of the tied corners; census doc 1aab796f (a cube mesh resting face down) keeps its t0 contact difference so (on MuJoCo's graph, all 168 are its bit for bit)

column3: keeps a step's contacts and constraint rows in one arena per mjData, sized by <size memory>, or else by nstack or a heuristic over the model's sizes, with room added for njmax rows and nconmax contacts (user_model.cc:5045-5078); a contact that does not fit is dropped with mjWARN_CONTACTFULL (mj_addContact, engine_core_constraint.c:214-231, and the collision driver's per-pair buffers, engine_collision_driver.c:1521-1526, :1890-1895, :2032-2038, :2119-2125), and when the rows do not fit none is made, with mjWARN_CNSTRFULL (arenaAllocEfc, engine_core_constraint.c:51-77); rows made are all dropped, with the same warning, when the island arrays do not fit (arenaAllocIsland, engine_island.c:64-70; clearIsland, :43); a stack that runs out while the rows are made stops the step ("mj_stackAlloc: out of memory", in mj_instantiateContact); and past mjMAX_EPA_ITERATIONS, EPA takes room for its polytope, 6 faces an iteration, from the arena's stack (ccd_allocate, engine_collision_convex.c:38-41), and a step it does not fit stops with "mj_stackAlloc: out of memory" (engine_collision_gjk.c:2304-2333). 100 spheres resting on a plane keep 93 contacts and make no rows under memory="100K", stop under 200K, and make their 400 rows then drop them under 270K; an ellipsoid sunk into a box runs under ccd_iterations of 10,000 and stops under 100,000; gen_collision_reference.py's mujoco_arena_limits asserts both

column3: a signed distance field is a geom of a plugin, over a mesh: a plane meets it through mjc_PlaneConvex, which walks the mesh's vertices (mjccd_support, engine_collision_convex.c:495, :598; :1042-1138) and lists a pair apart within the margin at its distance (:1056), a primitive or another field through mjc_SDF, a mesh through mjc_MeshSDF (engine_collision_driver.c:41-52); the geom-distance sensor takes the same functions (mj_geomDistance)
